author: TheHardcoreMARK
quote:
I understand why Ocarina of Time was revolutionary back in 1998, but playing it today is a frustrating experience.
The camera is clunky, the controls feel outdated, and the constant interruptions from Navi become annoying very quickly. Combat is repetitive, with too much waiting for enemies to expose themselves. Some puzzles are clever, but others feel unnecessarily confusing, especially in the Water Temple.
The world feels empty by modern standards, and the pacing is painfully slow at times.I respect its historical importance, but being influential doesn't automatically make a game enjoyable forever. Nostalgia shouldn't put a game above criticism.

1/10

author: TheHardcoreMARK
quote:
This is, without a doubt, the best GTA I've ever played. And what's incredible is how little it feels like the previous games.
For the first time in years, an open world doesn't feel like a plastic showroom where your interactions are limited to vending machines, scripted NPCs, and prostitutes.
You can try opening almost any door, and the world actually responds. Stealing cars is more challenging. Escaping the police takes real effort. You can interact with practically anyone, provoke strangers, be friendly, or simply observe how they react. Random encounters are more varied, unpredictable, and genuinely exciting.

And then there's STEALTH. Actual stealth in GTA! You can finally move bodies. You can no longer carry an entire Ammu-Nation store in your back pocket. And honestly? That's **** the biggest achievement is something else **** the first time, I don't feel like I'm just playing in a GTA world. I feel like I'm living in **** can take a shower, work out, buy food and drinks, walk into a bar ON YOUR OWN instead of watching a cutscene with your buddies, and actually order whatever you want. These might sound like small details, but together they completely transform the **** the story? The mission at the end of Act One alone puts half of today's blockbuster movies to shame in terms of writing, direction, tension, and sheer **** once, the protagonists feel like real people rather than empty shells designed to carry the plot forward. Their relationship and chemistry exist beyond scripted missions. 
They interact naturally, and you actually believe in **** amount of side content is ridiculous. Fishing, treasure hunting, racing, collecting items, random encounters, and countless little discoveries.I was literally just driving around when I saw a plane falling out of the sky. I followed it into the swamps, found the wreckage, a barely surviving guy, and the mysterious "cargo" he never managed to deliver.That's the kind of experience I'm talking about. Nobody told me to go there. I wasn't following a mission marker. I was just exploring, and the world gave me a story.
Every time I drive through these locations, I see a detailed, believable, living world. A world that doesn't just look real, but makes you want to believe in it.Vehicle damage is also vastly improved compared to GTA V, and the driving physics feel noticeably better. Cars have more personality, weight, and are simply more fun to **** finally, to everyone giving this game a 0/10 while claiming it's "just the same GTA again"...I get it. Not getting a PC release at launch must be **** judging a game you've never actually played says more about your frustration than the game itself.

Watching GTA VI on YouTube isn't playing GTA VI. Your entire gameplay experience consists of two buttons: pause and volume.This isn't GTA V 5.1. 
This is the GTA I've been waiting for all these years.

10/10.
